claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant on the present record, despite a known food safety inspection weakness, based primarily on aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a draft monitoring-and-rollback mitigation concept.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows no material weakness remains or shows an approved mitigation satisfying policy requirements.
Use suspicious when the record points toward launch readiness in part but omits a required support link or leaves a policy predicate unresolved.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance can support monitoring and documentation practices, but they do not override the internal disclosure policy.
Certification without material caveats is not supported by aggregate metrics alone when a named use-case limitation remains unresolved.
evidence_requests: Approved mitigation or risk acceptance showing owner, alert threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Materiality determination for the food safety inspection weakness in the named launch use case.
Final model-card or launch documentation showing the limitation is disclosed, or documented approval for not disclosing it.
Evidence that the weakness is resolved to target, not just offset by aggregate readiness.
specific_concerns: The unresolved weakness in the food safety inspection slice remains current and is concentrated in corrective-action note summarization.
The mitigation runbook is only draft and lacks required approval elements: accountable owner and alert threshold are still TBD.

Policy requires either no material weakness remaining or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for certification without material caveats; the available record does not show that threshold is met.
The model-card draft states there are no known material limitations, but reviewer commentary shows an unresolved question about whether this issue should be disclosed.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are not sufficient by themselves to eliminate a current disclosure obligation tied to a named launch use case.
unsupported_claims: That certification can be defended cleanly on the present record without resolving the disclosure predicate.
That draft monitoring and rollback planning is enough to remove the current disclosure requirement.
Any implication that the food safety inspection weakness is already covered by an approved risk acceptance.
